summary: The reader has the standard undergraduate computer science core: discrete mathematics (Cartesian products, permutations, induction, binomial coefficients, graphs, modular arithmetic, gcd, primes and division with remainder), linear algebra over the real and rational numbers (vector spaces, bases, matrices, eigenvalues, dot products, Gaussian elimination), calculus-level analysis (logarithms, exponentials, limits, geometric sums, roots of unity and Euler's formula), and algorithms and computer organization (Omega, Theta and little-o notation, recurrences, positional notation, two's-complement words). Not assumed are fields other than F_2, tensor products, bilinear forms, Gaussian integers, rings and groups, the integer Chinese remainder theorem, limit inferior and Newton iteration.

known.name: Logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The logarithm to base b is the inverse of the exponential b^x, satisfying log(xy) = log x + log y and log(x^c) = c log x, with lg denoting the base-2 logarithm and ln the natural logarithm.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling ⌈x⌉ is the smallest integer not less than x.

known.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
known.gloss: For a ratio r different from 1, the finite sum 1 + r + … + r^(k−1) equals (r^k − 1)/(r − 1).

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Induction proves a statement for every integer n at least n0 by proving it for n0 and proving it for n from its truth for smaller values (strong induction) or for the previous value (weak induction).

known.name: Recurrence relations for running times
known.gloss: A recurrence defines a cost T(n) in terms of costs at smaller sizes, and is solved by unrolling it into a sum or by substituting a guessed bound and checking it by induction.

known.name: Cartesian product of sets
known.gloss: The Cartesian product A_1 × … × A_t is the set of ordered tuples (a_1, …, a_t) with each a_i in A_i.

known.name: Permutation of a finite set
known.gloss: A permutation of a finite set is a bijection from that set to itself, and permutations can be composed and inverted.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set and equals n!/(k!(n−k)!).

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: Tuples are ordered lexicographically by comparing their entries at the first position where they differ, so the row-major order of an array is the lexicographic order of its index pairs.

known.name: Graphs, vertices and edges
known.gloss: A graph consists of a set of vertices and a set of edges, each edge joining two vertices, and two vertices are adjacent when an edge joins them.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: a ≡ b (mod m) means that m divides a − b, arithmetic on residue classes modulo m is well defined, and a has an inverse modulo m exactly when gcd(a, m) = 1.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprime integers
known.gloss: The gcd of a and b is the largest integer dividing both, two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1, and the extended Euclidean algorithm finds integers x and y with ax + by = gcd(a, b).

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer p at least 2 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p, and every integer at least 2 is a product of primes in exactly one way up to order.

known.name: Division with remainder
known.gloss: For integers a and b > 0 there are unique integers q and r with a = bq + r and 0 ≤ r < b, and then q = ⌊a/b⌋.

known.name: Limits of sequences and functions
aliases: limit as n tends to infinity
known.gloss: A quantity f(n) tends to L as n tends to infinity when, for every ε > 0, |f(n) − L| is less than ε for all sufficiently large n.

known.name: Nth roots of unity and polar form
known.gloss: The complex numbers z with z^n = 1 are e^(2πik/n) for k = 0, …, n−1, and Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ gives every nonzero complex number the polar form r·e^(iθ).

known.name: Vector spaces, bases and linear maps
known.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication by a field of scalars, a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and a linear map is a function between vector spaces that preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

known.name: Matrices, inverses and triangular matrices
known.gloss: A matrix records a linear map relative to chosen bases, matrix products correspond to composition of maps, an invertible matrix has an inverse, and a lower- or upper-triangular matrix has all entries on one side of the diagonal equal to zero.

known.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
known.gloss: A scalar λ is an eigenvalue of a square matrix M when Mv = λv for some nonzero vector v, and such a v is an eigenvector for λ.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and elementary row operations
known.gloss: Gaussian elimination reduces a matrix by adding multiples of rows to other rows and swapping or scaling rows, and it writes an invertible matrix as a product of elementary matrices.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product of x and y in R^n is the sum of the products x_i y_i, and two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.

known.name: Indicator vector of a subset
known.gloss: For a subset T of a finite index set, its indicator vector has entry 1 at the positions of the elements of T and entry 0 at all other positions.

known.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and XOR
known.gloss: Addition of bits is the exclusive-or operation, so 1 + 1 = 0, and the integers modulo 2 form the field F_2 with two elements.

known.name: Dyadic rational numbers
known.gloss: A dyadic rational is a number m/2^k with integers m and k, equivalently a rational number with a finite binary expansion.

known.name: Positional (radix) notation
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer n is written in base b as n = Σ d_j b^j with digits 0 ≤ d_j < b, and binary notation is the case b = 2.

known.name: Two's-complement integers
known.gloss: A w-bit two's-complement word represents the signed integers from −2^(w−1) to 2^(w−1) − 1, with its leading bit carrying weight −2^(w−1).
